panels.title: How to read the user range

options.content:
There is **no exact user count** without auth, so the truth is bracketed:

* **Unique users (lower bound)** — `mcp_users_active_estimate`, a HyperLogLog of
  `hash(IP + client)`. Users behind one NAT collapse together, so this **under**counts.
  It is an estimate (~1% error).
* **Unique sessions (upper bound)** — every reconnect is a new session id, so this
  **over**counts.

The real figure sits between the two lines on the panel to the right.

⚠️ **A deploy causes a temporary DAU dip.** The HLL sketches are in-memory and reset on
restart, then re-accumulate over the rest of the calendar window. That dip is an artefact,
not a real drop in users.

⚠️ **Single instance only.** Per-replica HLL estimates cannot be summed. Revisit before
scaling the SSE server past one replica.

panels.title: User range: unique users ↔ unique sessions
panels.description: Lower bound (HLL of hashed IP+client) vs upper bound (distinct session ids). Truth is in between.

panels.title: DAU / WAU / MAU
panels.description: HyperLogLog estimate per UTC calendar window. Resets at the window boundary; a restart mid-window undercounts until it re-accumulates.

panels.title: Concurrent sessions
panels.description: Sessions open right now, by client.

panels.title: Session length
panels.description: Median and p95 session lifetime.

panels.title: Bounce rate
panels.description: Share of sessions that initialized and then made zero tool calls — an onboarding/discovery problem, not a usage one.

panels.title: Engagement
panels.description: Mean tool calls and distinct tools per session.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Sessions by client. Unknown clients are bucketed as `other`; the label set is deliberately bounded.

panels.title: Client versions
panels.description: Version adoption, truncated to a semver prefix.

panels.title: Most-used tools (top 15)
panels.description: The headline usage question.

panels.title: Usage by product area
panels.description: `tool.category` — assets / evm / p2p / incentives / docs / resources / services.

panels.title: Tool latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Excludes `waited="true"` — serviceStatus{waitForRunning} blocks for seconds by design and would otherwise dominate the tail.

panels.title: Slowest tools (p95)
panels.description: Same exclusion as above.

panels.title: Errors by type
panels.description: Bounded taxonomy — messages are never recorded.

panels.title: Error rate by tool
panels.description: Tools whose calls fail most often, over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Overall error rate
panels.description: All tools, all error types.

panels.title: Compute jobs started
panels.description: Paid vs free.

panels.title: Compute job outcomes
panels.description: Terminal states only, deduped per jobId. 70/71 are both success.

panels.title: Chain usage
panels.description: Chains users actually target, from tools carrying a chainId.

panels.title: Escrow friction by caller
panels.description: `caller` separates an explicit escrow_preflight call from the implicit gates inside computeStart / serviceStart. The gate rates are the actionable ones — the user hit them without asking.

options.content:
Read top to bottom in the panel to the right:

1. `initializeCompute` — job priced
2. `escrow_preflight{caller="compute_gate"}` — can it be paid for?
3. `escrow_preflight{caller="compute_gate", result="ready"}` — escrow could back it
4. `compute.jobs.started` — actually launched

A large gap between steps 2 and 3 is payment friction, not disinterest. A gap between 3 and 4 means
escrow was fine and the start failed for another reason.

panels.title: Paid-compute funnel
panels.description: Counts over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Auth tokens created
panels.description: Paid-compute intent. The token itself is never recorded.

panels.title: Provider lookup hit rate
panels.description: DID → provider discovery. A falling rate means DDO resolution is degrading.

panels.title: Docs search hit rate
panels.description: Zero-result searches are a content gap. Query strings are never recorded.

panels.title: Escrow auto-fix outcomes
panels.description: `noop` = an existing authorization was below target and could not be raised automatically — advisory, not a fix.

panels.title: Incentives / node-operator tools
panels.description: Node-operator onboarding activity.

panels.title: Service start success rate
panels.description: Starts that were ever observed reaching Running (40). serviceStart is asynchronous — a doomed start still returns a serviceId and then dies in the background at the Locking step, so this gap is the ONLY visible signal of that failure.

panels.title: Service funnel
panels.description: Estimate → escrow gate → start → reached Running.

panels.title: Service outcomes
panels.description: Deduped per serviceId. NOTE the vocabulary differs from compute: here 40=Running, 70=Stopped, 75=Expired — 70 is NOT success.

panels.title: Service starts by image mode
panels.description: Only the mode is recorded — never the tag, checksum or Dockerfile body.

panels.title: Service lifecycle actions
panels.description: Post-start engagement: services that are actually used, not just started.

panels.title: serviceStatus latency: polled vs blocking wait
panels.description: `waited="true"` is the deliberate waitForRunning block. Kept separate so it never pollutes the latency SLO.

panels.title: libp2p connected peers
panels.description: Live CONNECTIONS, not discovered peers. DDO resolution depends on these; a gap in the series means the libp2p node was unreachable.

panels.title: Heap headroom
panels.description: Recording rule over the V8 heap metrics from the Node runtime instrumentation.

panels.title: Event-loop delay (p99)
panels.description: Rising delay means the process is saturated and every tool call gets slower.

panels.title: HTTP requests
panels.description: All HTTP requests handled by the Express app, by status code. Not filtered to /mcp: http_route is not reliably populated for these, so a filter would risk silently emptying the panel. In practice /mcp is nearly all of it.

panels.title: HTTP latency (p95)
panels.description: Transport-level latency, separate from per-tool latency.

panels.title: Order funnel (order_asset)
panels.description: order_asset is a multi-step state machine: it returns an unsigned tx, the caller signs and broadcasts, then calls back. This counts STEP TRANSITIONS, so the ratio of complete to needs_broadcast is how many order flows finish versus stall after a signature.

panels.title: Order completion rate
panels.description: complete / needs_broadcast over the range. A low value means users start ordering and abandon mid-signature.

panels.title: Downloads and fee quotes
panels.description: get_download_fees is purchase intent; download_asset_file is the consumption itself.

panels.title: DDO resolution hit rate
panels.description: Resolution is the precondition for ordering, compute and download alike, so a falling rate is a leading indicator for all three.

panels.title: DDO resolution by operation
panels.description: resolve / validate / check_files, split by hit and miss.

panels.title: Escrow transactions built
panels.description: deposit / withdraw / authorize. These tools build an UNSIGNED transaction and never broadcast, so this is intent to move funds, not settlement.

panels.title: Requests rejected before reaching a tool
panels.description: session_not_found means clients are holding session ids that died with the last restart. These requests move NEITHER mcp_tool_calls_total (no handler ran) NOR mcp_sessions_* (no session created), so this panel is the only place they appear.

panels.title: Activation latency (time to first tool call)
panels.description: The complement of bounce rate: mcp_sessions_empty counts sessions that never acted, this measures how long the rest took. Separates 'slow to start' from 'never started'.

panels.title: Errors by type (incl. auth)
panels.description: `auth` is its own bucket: ~44 tools take an auth token, and 'users cannot authenticate' needs a different fix from 'the network is down'. Without that rule these failures hide inside `internal`.

panels.title: Auth failure share
panels.description: Share of all tool errors that are authentication failures. A rising value points at token expiry or signing problems, not infrastructure.

panels.title: Persistent storage operations
panels.description: Bucket and file operations. No bucket id, file name or object key is ever recorded.

panels.title: Compute job observed duration
panels.description: First observed poll to terminal poll. A LOWER BOUND: the job was already running when first seen, and its terminal state is only noticed at the next poll.

panels.title: Service time to Running
panels.description: How long a start actually takes: escrow lock + image pull/build + vulnerability scan + container start. The expensive part of serviceStart.

panels.title: Poll depth per job / service
panels.description: How many status calls a client makes before something settles. This is the real cost of the polling UX — and the number waitForRunning is meant to reduce.

options.content:
`user.id` is on **spans only**, never on a metric — a per-user label would be a cardinality bomb
in Prometheus/Mimir.

To inspect one anonymous user's activity, open **Explore → Tempo** and run:

```
{ name =~ "tool\\..*" && span.user.id = "<hash>" }
```

Other useful queries:

```
{ name =~ "tool\\..*" && span.status = "error" }                     # every failing tool call
{ name = "tool.serviceStart" }                                      # who is starting services
{ name =~ "tool\\..*" && span.error.type = "onchain_revert" }        # on-chain failures
{ span.session.id = "<uuid>" }                                      # one whole session
```

Span attributes are limited to `tool.name`, `tool.category`, `session.id`, `user.id`, `status`
and `error.type`. Arguments, error messages and stack traces are never attached.
